methodology: counterexample-oriented: domains were selected specifically to stress costs uk4 introduces (spill/reload overhead, live ranges, stack frame, code growth, prologue/epilogue fraction, partial-unroll behavior), not a broad representative sweep.

smallA.rationale: Smallest problem where uk4 is legally available (K trip count 4, tile_k=4 gives finer K granularity than tile_k=8 would at this shape scale). Total problem size (4096 FLOPs) is far smaller than any domain tested in Stages 12-16 where uk4 was legal.
hypothesized_uk4_costs: spill/reload fixed overhead becoming a larger fraction of tiny total work
prologue/epilogue overhead becoming a larger fraction of total work
code footprint growth relative to genuinely tiny useful compute
smallA.measured_outcome: uk4 still won (351ns vs 500ns for uk1), despite real spills (10 stores/11 reloads) -- the worst spill count of any domain except rect. Hypothesized costs did not dominate at this scale.

highK.rationale: K trip count 16 -- double the largest previously tested (cube64, trip 8). uk4 here is a genuine PARTIAL unroll (4 remaining dynamic iterations), not a full collapse, distinguishing this from every uk4 case tested in Stage 16.
hypothesized_uk4_benefits: same repeated loop-control reduction mechanism as smaller domains
larger scheduling region per static loop body
hypothesized_uk4_costs: longer live ranges across a larger unrolled body
repeated spill traffic across more dynamic iterations if spills occur
highK.measured_outcome: uk4 still won (7.778ms vs 9.186ms for uk1). Zero spills at any factor -- the hypothesized repeated-spill-traffic cost never materialized because no spilling occurred at all.

rect_reused.category: C -- highest register pressure (reused from Stage 16)
rect_reused.rationale: No tile larger than 8x8x8 in any dimension has ever passed Stage 11 structural validation; no new tiling implementation was added for this experiment (explicit scope limit). rect_uk4 (18 spills, 20 reloads, 368 stack bytes) remains this project's strongest register-pressure case to date.
rect_reused.measured_outcome: uk4 still won in Stage 16 (0.004278ms vs 0.005185ms for uk1) despite the heaviest spilling ever measured.

code_size_stress_reused.category: D -- code-size/instruction-footprint stress (reused, treated as signal only)
code_size_stress_reused.rationale: perf is unavailable on this Pi (same limitation as Stages 13/16) so no instruction-cache-miss counter evidence can be collected. Code size is reported as a stress SIGNAL, never as a measured cache effect. A dedicated kernel-rotation stress harness (compiling/interleaving multiple distinct kernels to force real icache eviction) was NOT built this stage -- documented as an explicit untested dimension, not silently omitted.

structural_validation: all 6 new candidates (smallA/highK x uk1/uk2/uk4) passed Stage 11 structural validation before compilation; no candidate was rejected for structural, correctness, or unsupported reasons.
